mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in the past month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or 20-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3 percentage points in the past month signals weakening labor market conditions, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising unemployment are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past three months signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods of declining RSAFS are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past two months signals supply-side constraints, which leads to reduced output and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite negative signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of declining INDPRO are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in the past month signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or 5-day forward returns in periods of strong PAYEMS growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% and 1% respectively in the past month signals a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and RSAFS > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of strong HOUST and RSAFS growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in the past month, coupled with a CPI increase of less than 0.1%, signals a dovish monetary policy stance in a low inflation environment, which boosts equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL < 0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite positive signal, or 20-day forward returns in periods of dovish FED with low CPI are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over the past three months signals a strong economic growth environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day forward returns in periods of GDP growth are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
